Source Identity

title: Campus Safety and Security (CSS) Data
text:
Collection Context







Field
Description




Collector/producer
U.S. Department of Education, Office of Postsecondary Education (OPE)


Original purpose
To collect and publish information about crime and safety at U.S. colleges and universities, support federal reporting requirements, and provide students, families, and the public with information about campus safety.


Collection method
Annual Campus Safety and Security Survey completed by postsecondary institutions participating in federal student financial assistance programs. Institutions report statistics collected through campus security authorities and other applicable sources.


Record-creation event
An institution submits its annual Campus Safety and Security Survey, reporting criminal offenses, arrests, disciplinary referrals, and other required safety statistics for the applicable reporting years.

title: Campus Safety and Security (CSS) Data
text:
Observation and Scope







Field
Description




Unit of observation
Individual postsecondary institution or campus, with reported incidents categorized by offense, calendar year, and geographic location.


Population or objects represented
U.S. colleges and universities participating in Title IV federal student financial assistance programs.


Time period covered
Annual reporting, with each survey generally including crime statistics for the preceding three calendar years.


Geographic area coverage
United States, including participating postsecondary institutions nationwide.

title: Campus Safety and Security (CSS) Data
text:
Variables and Data Structure







Field
Description




Main variables/fields
Institution name and location; criminal offense categories; reported incidents of murder, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, motor vehicle theft, sexual offenses, and other crimes; hate crimes; arrests; disciplinary referrals; and campus geographic categories.


Data types included
Categorical variables, institution identifiers, calendar years, geographic classifications, and numerical counts of reported incidents.


Direct measurements
Institution-reported counts of criminal offenses, arrests, disciplinary referrals, and other incidents occurring within defined campus reporting locations.


Possible proxy variables
Reported crime counts as indicators of campus safety; arrests and disciplinary referrals as indicators of reported violations; changes in incident counts over time as indicators of trends in campus crime and safety.

title: Campus Safety and Security (CSS) Data
text:
Documentation







Field
Description




Documentation found
Campus Safety and Security Survey User’s Guide; Campus Safety and Security Data Analysis Cutting Tool User Guide; downloadable institutional data files; survey reporting instructions and definitions.


Stated collection details
Postsecondary institutions participating in federal student financial assistance programs submit annual campus crime and safety statistics under the Clery Act. Reported incidents are classified by offense type, calendar year, and geographic location. The Department of Education makes the information publicly available for institutional comparisons and analysis.
